where: §7 Data and software availability: "The data and software underlying this article are publicly available." … "prepared for deposit at [ZENODO DOI, minted on publishing the deposit], held until the licence position is settled" … "Whether they may be redistributed, and under which licence, is [CORPUS LICENCE: whether the derived corpus and the candidate pools may be redistributed, given DrugBank's terms]". Same placeholders in SI S1 and SI S14.
claim: The Data Availability Statement opens by asserting blanket public availability and then, in the same paragraph, leaves both the repository DOI and the redistribution licence as unresolved bracketed placeholders that survive into the submitted PDF.
why: Under ACS Research Data Policy Level 2 the DAS must state what is actually available and, where access is restricted, give the specific justified restriction. Here the first sentence is contradicted by the third and fourth: the deposit does not exist, its DOI is unminted, and the authors themselves do not yet know whether the deposit is lawful. SI S14 confirms the deposit is blocked ("the tool refuses to run without one: a Zenodo record cannot be withdrawn once published"), so if the licence determination comes back negative the DAS is simply false and no reader ever obtains the pools. A referee cannot evaluate an availability statement whose central term is an open question addressed to the authors themselves.
fix: Settle the licence question before resubmission and write the answer into the DAS and SI S1 as a determination, not a placeholder; mint the Zenodo DOI (a reserved DOI can be cited pre-publication) and give it. If DrugBank's terms forbid the deposit, say so explicitly and state exactly which components are withheld and on what access terms the remainder is obtainable.

where: §2.1 "The annotated substrate–metabolite pairs are assembled from four sources: ChEMBL, DrugBank, MetXBioDB and the GLORYx reference set" and SI S1, Table S1 (9,011 / 1,020 / 1,198 substrates); Introduction, "the artifacts sufficient to recompute any cell are released".
claim: Neither document describes how the corpus was assembled from the four sources or how it was partitioned, and the corpus itself is not released — so the dataset underlying every number is neither obtainable nor reconstructible.
why: Nowhere is it stated which ChEMBL tables or DrugBank fields yielded substrate–metabolite pairs, what filters or standardisation were applied to corpus records, how the four sources were merged and deduplicated when they disagree, or by what algorithm and seed the ~11,229 substrates were split 9,011/1,020/1,198. The split manifest pins the triple files by digest, which lets a reader detect a change but not rebuild the files. Because DrugBank 5.1.10 is CC BY-NC and the SI concludes the licences "do not combine", redistribution is at best doubtful — which leaves reconstruction as the only route, and the recipe for it is absent from both documents. The paper's headline claim that any cell can be recomputed is therefore not true for any cell: the coverage ceiling, the splits, the mined half of the rule bank and both trained stages all descend from a corpus a third party cannot produce.
fix: Add an SI section giving the full extraction procedure per source (queries/fields, inclusion filters, structure standardisation, cross-source deduplication and conflict resolution) and the splitting procedure (algorithm, seed, disjointness criterion), sufficient that a reader holding ChEMBL 34, DrugBank 5.1.10, MetXBioDB 1.0 and GLORYx 2020 can regenerate the three triple files and check them against the pinned digests.

where: §7 Data and software availability (repository contents list) against §3.9 "Every recall figure in this paper comes from one trained checkpoint" and SI S13 on LAGOM, "releases training code under Apache-2.0 but no fine-tuned checkpoint, so comparing would mean comparing against our own reimplementation".
claim: The trained generator and filter checkpoints are not among the released artifacts, so no reported GRAIL number can be reproduced — the exact omission for which the paper excludes LAGOM from comparison.
why: The DAS enumerates source code, split manifest, comparator predictions, harness, provenance sweep and preregistration; weights are not listed anywhere in either document. Every recall figure comes from one checkpoint (§3.9), and retraining is impossible because the corpus is unavailable (finding 2). A reader therefore cannot reproduce a single cell of Table 2, Table S5 or Table S3. Holding a comparator to a bar the manuscript does not itself clear is not defensible in a paper whose stated contribution is verifiability, and §4.3's "A reader therefore cannot presently verify any ranking in this literature" then applies to GRAIL too.
fix: Deposit the deployed generator and filter checkpoints (with their `arch` and rule-bank identifiers) alongside the candidate pools, and list them in the DAS; if a licence bars this, state that explicitly and withdraw the LAGOM criticism.

where: SI S13 Comparators, "BioTransformer is pinned by digest rather than by version string, because '3.0' names several builds: jar c70cad91, 115,415,197 bytes, upstream commit 6432cf88 of 2023-05-25, its 994 templates loaded at freeze time"; SI S10, "the 150 substrates shared with a further comparator"; Abstract, "against every comparator with predictions on the same substrates".
claim: BioTransformer is pinned in exhaustive detail, is used in the population analysis as an unnamed "further comparator", and yet appears in no table or figure, with no statement of why it was dropped.
why: S13 states a closing rule — "a comparator that could not be obtained is reported as unavailable with its reason, is not dropped silently" — and BioTransformer violates it in the other direction: it was obtained, run (S10's 150-substrate population can only be its intersection), and then silently omitted from Table 2, Figure 1 and Table S3. This also leaves the definition of the comparison set unreadable: "the 291 substrates on which every method predicts" does not say whether BioTransformer was one of the methods whose coverage fixed n=291. And the abstract's "every comparator with predictions on the same substrates" is either false or requires the unstated fact that BioTransformer predicts on only 150 of them.
fix: Name the further comparator in S10, and in S13 state plainly whether BioTransformer is in the comparison; if it is excluded, give the reason and the substrate count, and say explicitly whether it entered the definition of the 291.

where: SI S13, "MetaTox and MetaPredictor predictions are frozen per substrate and released with the code", against SI S13 on DeepCYP, "offers a web form and no models or API, so a comparison would mean submitting 1,170 substrates to a third-party server", and §3.1, "MetaTox alone, the incumbent web service this work set out to replace".
claim: Two of the three comparators carrying numbers in Table 2 are given no version, digest, or date of access, and the criterion used to exclude DeepCYP (web-only access) is contradicted by MetaTox's inclusion.
why: The SI list promises "comparator versions and digests"; SyGMa gets a version and BioTransformer a digest, while MetaTox and MetaPredictor — which supply four of the five non-GRAIL columns in Table 2 — get neither, nor an access date. MetaTox is a hosted web application whose model and templates can change without notice, so a frozen prediction file with no run date cannot be re-obtained or checked by anyone, and the numbers become unfalsifiable. Simultaneously, the paper's stated reason for excluding DeepCYP is that it is a web form, which is exactly what MetaTox is. The exclusion rule as written does not survive contact with the comparators actually used.
fix: State the MetaTox service run date (and server version if displayed) and the MetaPredictor commit/checkpoint and inference settings; restate the exclusion rule so it distinguishes DeepCYP from MetaTox on a ground other than web-only access, or drop that ground.

where: §2.3, "templates mined from the molecule-disjoint training split alone" (repeated verbatim in SI S4), against SI S1, "Molecular overlap between splits is non-zero and expected … 2,408 molecules occur in both train and test, and 243 test substrates appear as molecules in train".
claim: The training split from which half the rule bank is mined is described as "molecule-disjoint", which the SI's own overlap counts show it is not.
why: The splits are substrate-disjoint, as §2.1 correctly says; the SI then records exactly the molecular overlap that makes "molecule-disjoint" false, and the term is used only at the one place where it does most work — qualifying the provenance of the mined templates. A reader assessing whether the mined bank could encode test chemistry is given a stronger guarantee than the audit supports, in the two sentences where it matters. The SI's own framing ("Both counts are recorded so that neither is later discovered and mistaken for leakage") is undercut by the main text asserting the disjointness that those counts refute.
fix: Replace "molecule-disjoint" with "substrate-disjoint" in §2.3 and SI S4, and add one sentence stating whether any of the 243 test substrates appearing as train molecules contributed a mined template, and with what effect on the ceiling.

where: §2.1, "The comparison set carries no training contamination: 0 of its 291 substrates appear in train or validation under a canonical key", and SI S1, "A read-only audit verifies zero substrate overlap and zero annotated-pair overlap".
claim: The leakage audit's matching key is left undeclared ("a canonical key") and the audit tests only exact identity, in a paper whose thesis is that the matching criterion is a declared axis rather than a default.
why: The manuscript declares five matching criteria precisely because they disagree — SI S3 shows the verdict of the whole comparison moving at 6 of 9 budgets between them, and SI S3 documents two cases where distinct references merge under a looser key. The leakage audit is a matching problem of the same kind, and the paper applies to it an unnamed key, which is the practice it criticises elsewhere. Nor is any near-duplicate analysis reported: the audit tests identity only, while refs 15 and 16 (DataSAIL, Kretschmer) are cited two sentences earlier and are specifically about analogue and coverage bias defeating identity-based splits. A test substrate that is a salt, stereoisomer, tautomer or close analogue of a training substrate passes this audit unremarked.
fix: Name the key used by the audit (one of the five declared criteria) and report the overlap counts under all five, as is already done for the comparison; add a near-duplicate audit (e.g. maximum Tanimoto of each test substrate to the training set, with the distribution) and state the count above a stated threshold.

where: §2.3, "It is the deduplicated union of four curated collections together with templates mined from the … training split"; SI S4, identical sentence; §3.6, "the half of the bank with no expert provenance"; SI S4, "4,274 of 5,856 rest on a single training pair".
claim: The four curated rule collections that supply roughly 1,725 of the 7,581 deployed templates are never named, cited, versioned, or licensed anywhere in either document.
why: The bank is the object of the paper's second headline result (the 475-reference ceiling) and of the coverage census in Table 5, and the DAS treats it as a released artifact pinned by digest in the split manifest. A reader cannot tell whether the curated portion is SyGMa's own rules, GLORYx's, an in-house set, or something overlapping the comparators — which bears directly on the comparator-overlap argument the paper makes in §2.1 and SI S1. It is also a licence gap in a paper that devotes an SI subsection to licence incompatibility: the manuscript sets out the terms of four corpus sources while redistributing templates from four unidentified collections whose terms are not stated.
fix: Name and cite the four collections in SI S4 with their versions and licences, give the template count contributed by each after deduplication, and state whether any of them is shared with a comparator in Table 2.

where: §3.10 Runtime, Table 1 ("seconds, slowest 231.01"), Figure 3 ("did not finish in 600 s"), SI S12 ("A cache makes a repeated substrate run 16 to 47 times faster"), and §3.10 "Part of the speed-up is machine load".
claim: No hardware or software environment is specified anywhere for any timing, though runtime carries two registered predictions, a table, a figure and a 600 s cut-off.
why: P8 is adjudicated on a speed-up factor and P9 on an absolute median against a 10 s target; Figure 3's "did not finish" bucket is defined by a wall-clock deadline; and the authors themselves invoke "machine load" as an explanatory variable and divide it out by a factor of 1.73. None of this is interpretable, still less reproducible, without the CPU, core count, memory, and whether a GPU was used for the learned stages. Beyond RDKit 2022.09.5 no version is given for Python, PyTorch or torch-geometric, so even the numerical results are not pinned to an environment. SI S14 is titled "Provenance and reproduction" but contains provenance only — no commands, no environment, no expected runtimes.
fix: Add to SI S12 the machine specification (CPU model, cores, RAM, GPU if used) and to SI S14 an environment specification (Python and key package versions, or a lockfile/container digest) plus the concrete commands that regenerate the pinned artifacts.

where: §7, "are at github.com/doctawho42/GRAIL, and are available to reviewers at submission"; SI S6, "The register is released in full at github.com/doctawho42/GRAIL".
claim: The only pointer readers are given is a bare, mutable GitHub URL with no commit, tag, release, or archival DOI — the one artifact in the paper that is not pinned.
why: The manuscript's own apparatus pins 47 artifacts by producer hash and a split manifest by digest, precisely because a moving target cannot support a number. That discipline is then abandoned at the point of delivery: a reader in five years resolves this URL to whatever state the repository is in, or to nothing. It also makes the preregistration claim unverifiable — Table 4's register identifiers H7–H15 and SI S6's "stated with their thresholds so that a later result … cannot be a threshold chosen after the fact" rest entirely on a file in a repository the authors can rewrite, with no independent timestamp (OSF, Zenodo, a stated commit hash) offered in either document. Under ACS policy, software supporting a publication should be archived with a persistent identifier, not merely hosted.
fix: Archive the repository at the submitted state to Zenodo (or equivalent) and cite the versioned DOI plus the commit hash in the DAS; give the register its own timestamped deposit or, failing that, quote the commit hash and date at which each hypothesis was written.

where: SI S6, "Fifteen predictions are registered. Nine are reported in the paper as P1 to P9 … The remaining six … are stated with their thresholds so that a later result on any of them cannot be a threshold chosen after the fact"; SI listing in the main text, "the fifteen registered predictions, including the six this paper does not report".
claim: The SI promises the fifteen registered predictions with their thresholds and delivers a one-line topic list of six with no thresholds and no falsification conditions.
why: S6 names six topics ("a type-indexed rather than rule-indexed label space, reactivity and accessibility node features, learned abstention, …") and then asserts in the same paragraph that they "are stated with their thresholds" — but no threshold appears, in that section or anywhere else in the SI. The nine reported ones fare little better: Table 4 gives a threshold but neither document gives any falsification condition or the text as written. The whole preregistration claim is thereby deferred to an unpinned repository (previous finding), so the SI cannot discharge the function the main text assigns it.
fix: Print the fifteen predictions in an SI table with, for each, the statement as written, the threshold, the falsification condition, the population it was to be checked on, and the date or commit at which it was fixed.

where: Abstract, "five matching criteria and ten output budgets"; §2.7, "a grid of five matching criteria by eleven budgets: 0 of 55"; Table 4, row P4, "grid 5 × 10"; Table 2, Figure 1 and Table S3 all show nine budgets.
claim: The size of the evaluation grid is given three incompatible ways — ten, eleven (5×11=55), and 5×10 — while every displayed table uses nine budgets.
why: This is the paper's headline description of its own evaluation, and the discrepancy is not cosmetic: P4's pass criterion is "zero lost cells" over that grid, so whether it was checked over 45, 50 or 55 cells changes what the registered prediction asserts. It also breaks the manuscript's stated provenance rule. Checking the sources: `\numHOneOneCells` is macro-generated as 55 from a pinned artifact, while "ten output budgets" in the abstract and "grid $5\times10$" in `table_hypotheses.tex` are hand-typed literals that contradict it, and `\numCritBudgets` is 9. The checker that "refuses any numeric literal in the manuscript that is not on a short allow-list" did not catch either literal, so the gate is not doing the job the SI claims for it.
fix: Emit the budget count and the grid dimensions from the same pinned artifact as the 55, reconcile the abstract and Table 4 with it, and state in §2.7 which eleven budgets P4 covered and why the reported tables show nine of them.

where: §3.11, "337 need a transformation type the bank does not hold, 98 need a type it holds whose rule did not fire, and 40 cannot be typed", Table 5 and Figure 4, against SI S7, "Typing runs a maximum common substructure search under a wall-clock timeout and treats a cancelled search as untypeable, so the artifact is not byte-reproducible".
claim: The 337/98/40 decomposition, Table 5's invariance argument and the 42,554-template comparison all rest on a timeout-dependent, machine-dependent typing procedure, and the main text presents them as fixed quantities.
why: The non-reproducibility of typing is disclosed once, in SI S7, and bounded there only for Table S4's oracle. Nothing bounds it for the census: "40 cannot be typed" is by construction the timeout bucket, and on slower hardware — for which no specification is given (see the runtime finding) — that bucket grows and the 337 shrinks. Since 312 distinct types, the 0.8724 singleton mass, Table 5's four granularities and the "18 of 337" recoverable from synthetic templates are all derived from the same typing, a referee cannot tell how much of the paper's second headline result is hardware. The invariance demonstrated in Table 5 is invariance to the definition of a type, not to the timeout.
fix: Report the timeout value and the machine, re-run the census at a substantially longer timeout (or with the timeout removed) and give the resulting 337/98/40 split, and state the run-to-run variation of the census as SI S7 does for the oracle.

where: §7, "the train and validation candidate pools, holding every candidate the generator produced for every substrate of their population"; §5, "we release per-substrate predictions for every arm"; §7 repository list, "the frozen per-substrate predictions of every comparator".
claim: The deposit's contents are described by an undeclared population, and GRAIL's own per-substrate test predictions — on which every table depends — are not listed among the released artifacts.
why: Two problems in one sentence. First, "their population" is declared for the validation pool (the 300-at-seed-0 draw, 294/293) but never for the train pool: the training split holds 9,011 substrates, no training draw is among the three declared populations, and no cap or seed is given, so a reader cannot know what is being deposited. The repository's own `paper2/zenodo_manifest.json`, which §7 names, records the train pool at 349 substrates — under 4% of the split — with no cap or seed recorded, which is exactly the undeclared-subsample problem the paper's population discipline exists to prevent. Second, the DAS enumerates comparator predictions and the train/validation pools; GRAIL's per-substrate predictions on the 291-substrate comparison set and the 1,170-substrate evaluated test set appear nowhere in the list, although the Conclusions promise release "for every arm" and every cell of Table 2, Table S3 and Table S5 comes from them.
fix: Declare the train pool's population, cap and seed wherever the deposit is described, and add GRAIL's frozen per-substrate predictions for both evaluated populations and both operating modes to the enumerated release, or say where they already sit.

where: SI S5.2, "The estimator is selectable between a non-negative positive-unlabelled risk on logits and binary cross-entropy on probabilities; the released configuration uses the second", against SI S5.3, headed "The objective is positive-unlabelled" and stating "a rule-applicable product without an annotation is unlabelled".
claim: The SI states that the released filter is trained with plain binary cross-entropy and, in the next subsection, that the objective over the same products is positive-unlabelled.
why: These cannot both describe the deployed system: BCE on probabilities necessarily enters unannotated rule-applicable products as label 0, i.e. as negatives, which is precisely what S5.3 says is not done. S5.3's opening sentence concerns rules (the generator's down-weighting), but its heading and its product-level definition are general and immediately follow the filter subsection, so a reader reconstructing the filter's training cannot determine which loss and which label treatment produced the checkpoint that generated every reported number. The downstream claim that "precision is pessimistic by a bounded but unknown amount" is also stated as a consequence of the objective when it follows from annotation incompleteness regardless of loss.
fix: State in S5.2 the loss actually used for the released filter checkpoint and how unannotated applicable products are labelled under it, and retitle or rescope S5.3 so it is clear which stage the positive-unlabelled treatment applies to.

where: §3.9, "the generator and filter were retrained under 3 seeds and the whole pipeline re-evaluated on the full test split: macro recall@15 is 0.3437 with a standard deviation of 0.0099 … That study ran on an earlier operating point than the one reported here"; §3.11, "Applying the whole bank to every test substrate".
claim: The only training-variance estimate offered is three seeds on a superseded configuration evaluated on "the full test split", a population that is not one of the three the paper declares — and it is nevertheless used to scale the conclusions about P1, P2 and P3.
why: The manuscript's stated discipline is that populations are named and never mixed, and that a claim is made only where the interval on the relevant quantity excludes zero. Here the reference distribution for judging whether +0.0733 (P1) is "an order of magnitude larger than retraining noise" and +0.0092 (P3) is "within it" comes from a different operating point, a different population, and an SD from n=3, with the seeds themselves unnamed. §3.11 likewise measures the ceiling on "every test substrate" where §2.1 assigns it to the evaluated test set of 1,170. Neither is reproducible as stated, and the second is a mixing of populations of exactly the kind the paper undertakes to avoid.
fix: Name the three seeds; state whether "the full test split" means 1,198 or the declared evaluated test set of 1,170 and use the declared name throughout (including §3.11); and either rerun the seed study on the deployed operating point or drop the comparisons that use its spread as a yardstick for P1–P3.

where: §2.3, "Support is heavily skewed and mining is saturated: re-running the miner on the same split re-derives every template it derived before and none new"; §4.4, "Extending coverage requires new reaction corpora … and mining is saturated".
claim: The evidence offered for saturation is a deterministic re-run of the same miner on the same data, which is a reproducibility check and cannot fail for a deterministic procedure.
why: Re-running an idempotent extractor on identical input necessarily returns identical output; the observation establishes determinism, not that the template yield has plateaued. Saturation is a claim about the derivative of yield with respect to data, and it carries real weight here — it is the premise of the Discussion's conclusion that coverage cannot be extended without new corpora, and by extension of the search narrowed to enzymatic and regulatory sources.
fix: Either report a yield curve (new templates derived against fraction of the training split mined, e.g. at 25/50/75/100%) and let saturation stand on it, or restate the sentence as a determinism check and remove "saturated".

where: Main text SI listing, "the worked example's full ranked list"; SI S11 caption, "The first twenty of the 100 candidates … The complete ranked lists of both modes are in the released artifacts."
claim: The SI is advertised as containing the worked example's full ranked list and contains the first twenty of one hundred, deferring the rest to the repository.
why: Small in itself, but it is one of the enumerated deliverables of the Supporting Information, and the deferral is to the unpinned repository (see the archival finding), so a reader following the SI listing does not obtain what it names. The interactive mode's 18-candidate list would fit on the same page.
fix: Either print both complete lists in SI S11 (100 + 18 rows) or amend the main-text SI listing to say "the first twenty of the worked example's ranked list".

where: §6 Limitations, "applying the bank at depth two lifts the ceiling by about 0.012 at 8.5 times the candidate cost and is not deployed".
claim: A quantitative depth-2 result is asserted in Limitations with no population named, no interval, and no supporting table in the paper or SI.
why: Every other figure in the manuscript names its population and, where it is a difference, its interval; this one names neither, and "about 0.012" is the only hedged number in a paper that is otherwise exact. It also bears on the paper's second headline result, since it is the one measurement addressing whether the 475-reference ceiling is a single-step artefact.
fix: Give the population (presumably the evaluated test set), the exact ceiling with and without depth 2, and the candidate counts, in one SI line.
